source.title: Northern Whig, 20 September 1946, p. 3 ("Rural council nominations")
source.publisher: Northern Whig (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Contested votes from the Belfast News-Letter results (5 October 1946, p. 3); unopposed returns from the Northern Whig (20 September 1946, p. 3); Groomsport withdrawal from the Belfast News-Letter (21 September 1946, p. 3).

note: Triennial election of the Newtownards Rural District Council, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. Four divisions were contested; Groomsport became unopposed on Thomas Campbell's withdrawal, and fourteen divisions were uncontested. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Party (w19-fixes2, 19 Nov 2026): the recorded UUP rested on a printed label 'U.' that the Northern Whig list of 20 September 1946, p. 3 (page image, w19-bna-fix) does not print for this council, so Party_As_Printed is cleared. No party is recorded (unknown), as there is no consistent evidence: his returns before and after (Alexander Adair 1939, Alex. Adair 1952) carry no label. Renamed from 'Donaghadee' to Donaghadee Rural (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Donaghadee Rural; the rounds were filed as Donaghadee (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1946, 1952, 1958); Donaghadee Rural (1939). This round was filed as 'Donaghadee', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (donaghadee) answers with a redirect to this one.
